svg.title: Lease Exit Map for the Leaseholder
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-lease-exit-counterparties; chapter number: 11; chart type: org_architecture; title: Lease Exit Map for the Leaseholder; subtitle: Who sets the exit price when a lease ends early; caption: The leaseholder sits between the landlord's buyout terms, legal advice on the duty to re-rent, a replacement-tenant offer, and statutory exits such as SCRA.; assumptions note: Termination fees of 1 to 3 months rent and a buyout around two months rent are typical figures cited by the speakers; Florida caps liquidated damages at two months under Statutes 83.595.; note: Drawn from DoorLoop (DMY8aqSWFmQ), Tenant Law Group, PC (mXtFESh8Jwc), 60SecondLaw (X_XeyY10oQE), Adulting Shouldn't Suck (07RfH5S46pg), and Better Call Kal (2ZipHRbP_7U).; center: role: Leaseholder on the master lease; headcount: Single leaseholder entity; focus: No move-out and no rent stoppage until a termination agreement states the amount, move-out date, and that no further rent is owed.; spokes: role: Landlord or property manager; type: Counterparty; kpi: Buyout around two months rent; fees typically 1 to 3 months; role: Local landlord-tenant attorney; type: Advisor; kpi: Direction on the state duty to re-rent, often free; role: Replacement tenant; type: Negotiating chip; kpi: Proposed alongside an early-termination penalty offer; role: Military orders under SCRA; type: Statutory exit; kpi: Lease ends 30 days after the next rent date; no fees
